open_points.subject: M05 Implementation / M08 AdmissionVerdict / action "author a function contract or implementation"
open_points.text: "author a function contract or implementation ... the version with its identity — an existing one when the content is equal" + "admit and activate | kernel, when an implementation is submitted"
open_points.question: If an agent submits code equal to an existing implementation, is that still a new submission event that must run admission over the current corpus (and possibly create a new Activation), or is it only a lookup returning the existing implementation with no admission/activation change?
options: Equal-code submit triggers admission again against current corpus
Equal-code submit is deduplicated lookup only; no new admission
Equal-code submit triggers admission only when no current admitted verdict over current corpus exists
open_points.default_guess: Treat equal-code submit as a submission event and rerun admission over the current corpus.

open_points.subject: M03 ContractVersion / M02 Slot current contract
open_points.text: "A slot's current contract version is the one issued last" + "author ... existing one when the content is equal"
open_points.question: When a request names a slot and matches an older (non-current) contract version exactly, does returning that existing version change which contract version is considered current for the slot?
options: No; current changes only when a newly issued version is created
Yes; any successful author request makes the returned version current
Request matching older version is refused to preserve monotonic current
open_points.default_guess: No change; only newly issued versions advance the slot's current contract version.

open_points.subject: Run lifecycle (M19) vs owner refusal effect action
open_points.text: "While some nodes wait, independent branches keep running" and "When the owner refuses an effect, the run ends `refused`"
open_points.question: If the owner refuses one effect while other branches are runnable or in progress, does the kernel stop all further scheduling immediately (hard terminal), or may in-progress node attempts finish before the run is marked ended?
options: Immediate terminal stop: no further node work once refusal is decided
Allow already-started attempts to conclude, but schedule nothing new
Branch-local refusal only, with global end after remaining runnable work drains
open_points.default_guess: Immediate terminal stop after refusal decision; do not schedule additional node work.

open_points.subject: M24 EffectApproval cardinality for a run/node/map
open_points.text: M24 has `run_id`, `node_id`, `map_index`, `binding_id`, status lifecycle, and says a mismatched approved unused approval "stays `approved` and unused ... kernel then ... requests a new approval"
open_points.question: What cardinality constraints apply to approvals at the same run/node/map (especially for retries/resends): can multiple historical `approved` records coexist, and can more than one `requested` approval be open at once?
options: Many historical approvals allowed; at most one `requested` open per run/node/map
Many approvals allowed including multiple concurrent `requested`
Exactly one approval record per run/node/map, reused across retries
open_points.default_guess: Allow multiple historical approvals but enforce at most one open `requested` approval per run/node/map.
